n: The heart of the fourth Servant Song. The speakers marvel: who would have believed what we’ve heard? To whom has God’s saving power been shown? Abinadi quoted this whole chapter to King Noah’s priests (Mosiah 14) and explained it as a prophecy of Christ.
He grows up like a tender shoot from dry, unpromising ground. Nothing about his appearance draws attention or marks him as a king. Jesus grew up in humble Nazareth, unrecognized by most.

f.w: as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground

n: He was despised and rejected, a man of sorrows familiar with grief. People turned their faces away and didn’t value him. Jesus experienced rejection from His own people and abandonment by His friends.

f.w: a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief

n: He carried our griefs and sorrows—yet we assumed God was punishing him. Alma teaches that Christ took upon Himself not only sins but also pains, sicknesses, and infirmities, so He knows how to help us. Matthew links this verse to Jesus’s healings.

f.w: Surely he hath borne our griefs

f.g: Hebrew ḥoli—sicknesses; sorrows here means pains.

n: He was pierced for our rebellions and crushed for our sins; the punishment that brought us peace fell on him, and by his wounds we are healed. This is the core of the Atonement: Christ suffered in our place.

f.w: he was wounded for our transgressions

f.g: Welts or wounds from a whip.

n: We all wandered off like sheep, each choosing our own way, and the Lord laid all our sins on him. No one is excluded from either the problem or the remedy.

f.w: All we like sheep have gone astray
the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all

n: Mistreated and afflicted, he didn’t say a word in his defense—like a lamb led to slaughter or a sheep silent before shearers. Jesus stayed silent before His accusers; Philip taught the Ethiopian about Jesus from this very verse.

f.w: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter

f.g: Silent, unable or unwilling to speak.

n: Through oppression and an unjust trial he was taken away. Who even considered his fate? He was cut off from life for his people’s sin. Abinadi explained “his generation” as those who become Christ’s seed (Mosiah 15).

f.w: cut off out of the land of the living

n: They assigned him a grave with criminals, yet he was with a rich man in his death—though he had done no violence or deceit. Jesus died between two thieves and was buried in the rich Joseph of Arimathea’s tomb.

f.w: he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death
neither was any deceit in his mouth

n: Startlingly, it was the Lord’s will to let him be crushed. As he becomes an offering for sin, he will see his offspring and live long, and God’s purpose will succeed. The Father’s plan required the Son’s sacrifice; after it comes resurrection and “seed”—those redeemed.

f.w: it pleased the LORD to bruise him

f.g: A hint of life after death—fulfilled in the Resurrection.

n: After his anguish he will see the result and be satisfied. By knowing him, many will be made righteous, because he bears their sins.

f.g: Travail = intense labor, anguish, as in childbirth.

f.w: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many

n: God gives him a victor’s share because he poured out his life to death, was counted among criminals, carried many people’s sins, and pleaded for sinners. Jesus prayed for those crucifying Him and still intercedes for us.

f.w: he was numbered with the transgressors

f.g: Share the plunder after a victory—a sign of triumph.
